thread:
incident-bot: Paging @maria (on-call): high error rate and 95th latency spike on /v1/embeddings-canary (eu-west-1) detected by monitors. Aggregate latency 95p = 3.2s, normal 95p = 0.25s. 20% error rate 5m window.

alex: saw this from canary dashboard, started 12:42 UTC. stack traces show OOM-ish messages and lots of `batch_resize` warnings.

maria (on-call): acknowledge. looking now. which commit went to canary?

alex: deploy from 1901231234 — change was `dynamic_batching: true` + knob that increases max_batch_size based on queue length. quick diff: `server/batcher.py` changed scheduling loop.

carla (support): customers seeing slow responses in eu-west. support queue has 3 P1s mentioning timeouts for batch upload endpoints. No data exfiltration.

maria (on-call): ok immediate plan: 1) flip feature flag to disable dynamic batching on canary 2) if no quick improvement, revert commit and redeploy canary 3) notify support & estimate RTO.

maria (on-call): @deploy-bot please kill flag `ff/embeddings_dynamic_batching` on canary pool.

deploy-bot: Received request to toggle feature flag `ff/embeddings_dynamic_batching` for pool `canary-eu-west-1`. Applying... ✅ Flag disabled on 3/3 canary hosts.

maria (on-call): monitoring-bot, push a one-off check.

monitoring-bot: Canary latency 95p dropped to 1.1s after flag kill, error rate down to 8% (5m). Still above baseline and memory creeping.

alex: looks better but memory still climbs over several minutes. I suspect a path in the new batching code that grows buffers. need quick revert.

maria (on-call): agree. @sre-lead we need a roll-back of commit 1901231234 from canary only. Can someone take deploy? Also @ben (next-oncall) heads-up for handoff in 30m.

sre-lead: I'll patch and roll single-commit revert to canary, then watch for stabilization. Alex pls attach the exact revert command.

alex: git commands:```bash
git checkout -b revert/1901231234
git revert --no-edit 1901231234
# run unit tests (fast)
git push origin revert/1901231234
# trigger canary deploy in CI: ./scripts/deploy.sh --env=canary-eu-west-1 --image=sha:abcd1234-revert
```

maria (on-call): deploy when ready. I'll coordinate post-deploy checks and notify support.

sre-lead: starting revert deploy now. CI passed quick smoke. Deploying to 3 canary nodes, rolling update. deploy-bot will post status.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for image sha:abcd1234-revert. Rolling update 3 nodes: node-01 -> draining, node-02 -> draining, node-03 -> draining.

deploy-bot: node-01 updated ✅ node-02 updated ✅ node-03 updated ✅ Canary deployment complete.

maria (on-call): monitoring-bot, give me 1m baseline.

monitoring-bot: 1m: latency 95p = 0.28s, error rate = 0.5%, mem stable at expected baseline.

carla (support): Heads-up to support: ETA for resolution 12m. I'm updating the three P1 tickets with summary and mitigation: disabled dynamic batching flag and reverted commit to canary; monitoring shows healthy.

ben (next-oncall): I'll take over watch for the next 2 hours. If anything regresses, page me with `@ben (next-oncall) urgent`.

maria (on-call): handing off to @ben — brief: bad canary rollout changed batching policy causing memory growth and latency; flag killed gave partial relief; revert fully restored baseline. No customer data loss. Current status: canary healthy, preparing to promote revert to prod cutoff window at 16:00 UTC pending further soak.

ben (next-oncall): ack. I'll keep an eye on eu-west and the rollout plan.

alex: I'll open a PR to add a safety cap in the batching code and an integration test for queue growth. Also will document rollback steps in the runbook.

maria (on-call): postmortem action items: 1) stricter canary limits (max batch size caps), 2) test for memory regressions in CI, 3) feature flag auto-kill if memory growth > X% in 5m, 4) update runbook with specific `git revert` + deploy commands.

carla (support): letting customers know monitoring will update if we promote to prod; for now tickets set to resolved with notes.

incident-bot: Incident closed for now: status=resolved, severity=sev2, time_to_recover=00:18:23. If further regressions, please reopen thread. :white_check_mark:

ben (next-oncall): leaving a note — will watch until 16:30 UTC then hand back. Good job team. :thumbsup:
